name: Forge
summary: One window for many small local apps: games, creative tools, readers and research helpers, each its own little web server.
env_about: Variables every app's backend gets ('env' below) and those one app gets (its entry's 'env'). {data}, {config}, {cache}, {state} and {logs} are Forge's folders on the system it runs on (forge_portable.data_dirs); {port:<app>} is that app's port. Mostly they move each app's data out of the home folder into Forge's own data folder.

runtime.about: Relocatable CPython builds from python-build-standalone (Astral), the same ones uv installs. A target's runtime_sha256 is the digest GitHub lists for that file; the build refuses a download that does not match.
runtime.leave_out_about: Parts of the runtime a release never uses: the standard library's test suite (which holds sample private keys), IDLE, turtle demos, Tk, its C test modules and pip (a bundle installs nothing).

included: three.js 0.186.0 (MIT, the three.js authors): shared/vendor/three, apps/cosmos/static/vendor
xterm.js 6.0 and its fit, search and web-links add-ons (MIT, the xterm.js authors): apps/terminal/static/vendor
skip: key or password written in a setting
third_party.about: The runtime, packages and downloaded assets are read for secrets and this laptop's real values, not for personal patterns (authors' addresses). These secret patterns are skipped there too: library docs are full of user:password@host and key = '...' examples, and compiled files hold byte runs that look like them. Real key formats, private keys and the known values are still looked for.

packages.source_only_about: Pure-Python packages published only as source: built into wheels here once, then installed like the rest.
packages.leave_out_about: Installed files taken out again, from inside site-packages: pyobjc's own tests and debug symbols (about 20 MB on macOS), and the command scripts pip writes to bin/, whose first line names the building machine's Python (the launcher never runs them).

targets_about: One entry per download. uv_platform is the platform uv resolves and installs wheels for (uv pip install --python-platform), so every bundle is built on Linux with each package's own per-system dependencies; macos_min is the oldest macOS the wheels may need. launch: files from release/launch/ copied to the bundle's top (name in bundle: file there); forge_installer.py is the Linux install and uninstall (forge --install). setup: an Inno Setup script in release/launch/ that build.py turns into Forge-Setup-<version>.exe beside the zip when Inno Setup is installed under Wine (FORGE_ISCC, else the Wine prefix's Program Files); without it the zip is the whole Windows download. app_bundle: wrap the bundle in Forge.app (macOS).
ship_about: What a bundle holds: these paths plus apps/<name>/ for every app included below, minus anything leave_out matches (fnmatch on the path from the Forge folder; * also crosses /). shared/ ships by allowlist (critic round 1 of the 0.2 plan): only the files and folders named here, the ones the hub and the shipped apps use, so a new file there (often the owner's own tool or notes) stays out until it is added. The build stops when a shipped file names /shared/<file> that is not shipped.
leave_out_keep_about: Paths that ship although a leave_out pattern matches them: Exolab's data/tests/ holds the bench tests its tester runs (data, not code tests).
leave_out_about: tests, developer settings and handoff docs; generated hub files (the launcher makes them per request); shared parts only the owner's tools use (Live2D avatars under their own licence, Blender and Godot bridges, saved logins, session titles, a site downloader, chat attachments, the voice hotkey and its wake words, the voice script (the Voice app is not shipped, so Afterglow shows no Read aloud or mic button), the chat, session and avatar views, web search and capture, the session launcher and opener, the asset fetcher); Drift Peaks' bundled music (commercial tracks); the owner's own jobs and notes (Dossier's batch-job file, its run log, its USB copy tool); Arcade's physics sweeps, which are tests; the shared asset and sound packs, of which an app ships only what its 'assets' names; the keyring and Google Drive helpers, which only Office (not shipped) uses.

scrub.about: Text swapped in the release copy only, never in the source: home folders and mounted drives in examples, comments and defaults a release overrides, and notes that point at the owner's own setup (his assistant's files, the job number that built a file), and script tags for shared parts the release leaves out. Patterns are Python regular expressions; {home} stands for the building account's home folder, matched as it is. After the swaps no 'forbid' pattern may match any shipped file or path.

apps_about: Every app in apps/, in the release or not (why); a bundle and the source tree carry only the included ones. An included app may name what it needs on one system ("cut: why" leaves it out of that bundle), extra packages, variables for its backend (env) the parts of shared/ only it uses (assets: folders in git shipped with it, CC0 unless their own manifest says otherwise) and files kept out of git that the build downloads, pinned by SHA-256 (downloads; credit goes into THIRD-PARTY.txt).

features_about: Each hub feature per system: native, replaced, fallback or cut, with why after a colon. A feature that is neither native nor replaced has its controls hidden (hide: CSS selectors), its home widgets taken out of the widget menu (widgets: widget kinds), its settings left out of Settings (settings, settings_groups), whole Settings pages left out (settings_pages: their data-section ids) with the Reset groups that touch them (reset_groups), the help under a shown setting reworded (words: setting key to text, for help that names something cut), a Reset group's description reworded (reset_words: group id to text) and theme values set (theme). readme: false keeps it out of a bundle's README (it concerns something the release does not ship). tester: what a bundle's README says about it, in plain words (one text, or one per system); a feature with none is not in a bundle's README, whose list is for testers (the developer reasons stay here and in the source README).

words.away_minutes: After this long with no keyboard or mouse, Forge draws at 15 frames a second with no visualiser and half the particles, and after four times as long the moving effects stop. Touching anything brings it all back: at once on the home screen, within a few seconds inside an app. Nothing changes while anything can be heard playing. 0 turns it off.

words.forge_layout: New folds related apps into places with tabs, opens apps in Simple and reads at 15 px. Classic is Forge from before that: every app its own tile, each app's own text size and the mode you left it in. Your own choices below are kept for when you switch back.

licence_about: The licence's name (an SPDX id such as MIT), with a LICENSE file in release/source/ mapped in source.top. Empty: none chosen yet, and the README says all rights are reserved.

source.about: The source tree (build.py --source-tree): what ships, plus the paths in add (not filtered by leave_out), with the files in top copied to the tree's own paths (README.md filled in by build.py).
